title: skilldrop packs.json
$comment: RFC-0001 / RFC-0026 / RFC-0029 / RFC-0032 / RFC-0033. Packs and outcomes are METADATA ONLY — skills never move out of flat skills/<name> folders. RFC-0033: each skill and loop sits in exactly one pack; shared skills live in `core`, which other packs pull in via `requires`. Packs answer WHO needs a skill; outcomes answer WHY someone opened the catalogue. Both get the same two-way membership check in validate.py.

packs.description: Role-based bundles. Keys are pack names.

description.description: One line — who this pack is for.

display_name.description: RFC-0032. Human title for the pack's page and plugin entry. Same key as agent-ready-repo's pack.toml.

keywords.description: RFC-0032. Search terms, copied into the plugin entry.

links.description: RFC-0032. Catalogue-facing links; `documentation` is the pack's page.

first-value.description: RFC-0032. What to try first after installing, how to tell it worked, and what to do if it didn't. Key names match agent-ready-repo's [pack.first-value].

skills.description: Real skill folders. Every skill must appear in at least one pack.

requires.description: RFC-0033. Packs installed together with this one (in practice, `core`). One level only: a required pack may not itself require.

loops.description: RFC-0028. Real loops/ folders. Every loop must appear in at least one pack.

outcomes.description: The catalogue's second browse axis. A browse aid only — never an install unit; the CLI takes no --outcome.

description.description: The chip's tooltip on the catalogue site.
